title: Laredo man among five noncitizens charged in South Texas election-integrity cases
excerpt: Federal prosecutors say a 29-year-old Laredo man is among five non-U.S. citizens charged with voting-related offenses, in cases announced four days before Election Day.
content:
A 29-year-old Laredo man is among five non-U.S. citizens charged in South Texas election-integrity cases announced by federal prosecutors on October 30, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Texas.

Diego Benavides Rodriguez, 29, of Laredo, is charged in Laredo with voting by an alien in a federal election and with falsely claiming U.S. citizenship, prosecutors said. The cases allege he voted in the 2024 federal election.

The illegal-voting charge carries up to one year in prison and a $10,000 fine if convicted, while the false-claim charge carries up to five years and a $250,000 fine, according to the Justice Department release.

The other defendants are Ali Khan, 33, of La Porte; Mohammed Omar Hassan, 61, of Houston; Jose Vazquez-Mendoza, 51, of Port Isabel; and Karen Hinojosa-Martinez, 37, of McAllen. Prosecutors said Khan, Hassan and Rodriguez allegedly voted in 2024, Hassan also allegedly voted in 2022, and Vazquez-Mendoza allegedly voted in a 2022 special election for Texas' 34th Congressional District. Hinojosa-Martinez was indicted by a McAllen grand jury on a charge of lying on immigration documents after allegedly voting in a federal election.

The FBI and Homeland Security Investigations investigated the cases with assistance from the Texas Attorney General's Office and U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services, prosecutors said.

An indictment or criminal information is only an accusation, not evidence, and each defendant is presumed innocent unless convicted. The announcement came four days before Tuesday's November 3 general election, when Webb County voters will decide local, state and federal races.
